title: Groupe de Barsotti-Tate et cristaux (jusqu’en été 1969) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: abelian schemes A over a base of characteristic p, with étale Tate module T_p(A)_ét, the Tate module of the étale quotient of A[p^∞]. This is a lisse Z_p-sheaf whose rank is the p-rank. On the previous page Grothendieck builds a canonical isomorphism (*) α_A : det T_p(A)_ét → det T_p(A^∨)_ét. The construction goes as follows.
- Choose a polarization (or symmetric isogeny) φ̃ : A → A^∨.
- Coker T_p(φ̃)_ét is identified with (Ker φ̃)(p)_ét.
- Ker φ̃ is autodual, so its étale part is Cartier-dual to its multiplicative (radiciel) part. This gives the order relation ord(Ker φ̃)(p)_ét^2 = ord Ker φ̃(p) = deg φ̃ (p-part).
- So det T_p(φ̃)_ét, divided by the appropriate power of p, is an isomorphism independent of φ̃. It is compatible with base change and functorial for automorphisms, with det T_p(u)_ét · det T_p(u^*)_ét = 1 for u ∈ Aut(A). It is false for general endomorphisms.

This page continues that discussion in four parts.
(i) If A is over an algebraically closed field (connected base), the isomorphism is 'functorial' only in a twisted sense with respect to isogenies between abelian schemes of the same dimension. The two functors A ↦ det T_p(A)_ét and A ↦ det T_p(A^∨)_ét do not have the same variance in A.
(ii) The marginal and boxed insertion records the correct replacement for functoriality. For an isogeny u : A → B, det T_p(u)_ét · det T_p(u^∨)_ét = degree, read through α_A and α_B, i.e. (p-part of) deg u times the identity. This is a 'determinant of isogeny' formula.
(iii) c) To check: α_{A^∨} = α_A^{-1}, up to sign, under A^∨∨ = A. He also notes the behaviour under some operation on A (illegible).
(iv) d) To check: the isomorphism between rank-one objects ( )^A_ét → ( )^{A^∨}_ét induced by α_A agrees with the one coming from duality in De Rham cohomology described earlier. These are presumably determinants of the unit-root/étale part attached via the Dieudonné crystal / H^1_DR to T_p(A)_ét. This is the comparison of the étale-Tate-module picture with the crystalline/De Rham picture, central to the Barsotti–Tate/crystals programme of the notebook.

The page ends the notebook with two verifications left open: c) and d).
errors: The formula det T_p(u)_ét · det T_p(u^∨)_ét = deg u (and the previous page's ord(Ker φ̃)_ét^2 = ord Ker φ̃) holds only when Ker u (resp. Ker φ̃) has no local-local part, e.g. for ordinary A. In general the left side has p-adic valuation v(ord (Ker u)_ét) + v(ord (Ker u)_mult) ≤ v(deg u). The normalization of α_A should use ord (Ker φ̃)_ét rather than a square root of the degree. Unless an ordinarity hypothesis was imposed in an earlier, unseen part of the notes, this is a gap.
Claims c) (α_{A^∨} = α_A^{-1} up to sign) and d) (compatibility with De Rham duality) are explicitly left unverified ('à vérifier').

ideas.what: Canonical isomorphism det T_p(A)_ét ≅ det T_p(A^∨)_ét, normalized via any polarization and independent of it
ideas.modern_name: determinant of the étale (unit-root) part of A[p^∞]; comparison of p-adic characters of A and A^∨
ideas.usually_credited_to: folklore; unit-root crystal theory of Katz (1973) and Deligne ('Cristaux ordinaires', 1981)

ideas.what: Determinant formula for an isogeny: det T_p(u)_ét · det T_p(u^∨)_ét = deg u (p-part), via α
ideas.modern_name: degree of isogeny in terms of étale/multiplicative parts of the kernel

ideas.what: Compatibility of α with De Rham duality for H^1_DR
ideas.modern_name: compatibility of the unit-root / Dieudonné crystal description with the De Rham pairing
ideas.where_published: related themes in Grothendieck's 1970 ICM talk and 'Groupes de Barsotti–Tate et cristaux de Dieudonné' (1974)

missed.claim: Two verifications are left open at the end of the notebook: that α_{A^∨} = α_A^{-1} up to sign, and that α agrees with De Rham duality. These are routine consistency checks, and their content is subsumed by later theory of unit-root crystals and Dieudonné duality.
missed.quote: Il faudrait vérifier que α_{A*} = α_A^{-1} [sauf signe (?)...] ... est bien celui décrit plus haut de la dualité en cohomologie de De Rham (à vérifier ...)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor. It documents Grothendieck's 1969 attention to determinants of étale Tate modules and their crystalline counterparts, which is of historical interest only.

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine consistency checks on a canonical determinant isomorphism. Its existence follows from local existence of polarizations, and later unit-root/Dieudonné theory absorbs it. Nothing here appears to be a missed result.
transcription_corrections: Marginal insertion likely reads 'vaut aussi pour isogénies (si "dualité") pour schémas abéliens de même dimension' rather than 'S.d.A.', which is probably 'Sch. Ab.' = schémas abéliens.
Boxed formula: 'det T_p(u)_ét det T_p(u^∨)_ét = degré' (for an isogeny u).
'$\alpha_{A^*}$' denotes the dual abelian scheme A^∨ (Grothendieck writes A* for the dual).
In d), the objects are probably det-type rank-one objects '(det)^{A}_{ét} → (det)^{A*}_{ét}'.
First line likely begins '[Si] A connexe ...' or 'Mais si A ...'.
